options.content:
| | |
|---|---|
| Maps | The [USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/national-geospatial-program/historical-topographic-maps-preserving-past) (public domain): Furnace Creek at 1:250,000 (1908), Bullfrog at 1:125,000 (1942), Bullfrog at 1:62,500 (1954) and Beatty at 1:24,000 (1987), the USGS's georeferenced GeoTIFF scans |
| Placing | Each sheet clipped at its neatline and moved from NAD27 to WGS 84 with NOAA's grids, in Web Mercator. A scan's own georeferencing can be off by a few tens of metres |
| The 1:1 map | The 1987 sheet over the town of Rhyolite at 2.5 m a pixel, 2.85 by 2.22 km, in eight stages of five years from 1987: torn along a fractal field (seeded 1946, the year of the story) and bleached toward the sand. Drawn, not observed |
| Animals | [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org) occurrences of animals in the town with coordinates and a year, under CC0 or CC BY 4.0 (CC BY-NC records left out): 537 records of 76 kinds, from 1913 to 2026, named after the GBIF backbone. Each record's dataset is in its tooltip |
| Rhyolite | The magenta ring on every map: Rhyolite where the USGS's [Geographic Names Information System](https://www.usgs.gov/tools/geographic-names-information-system-gnis) puts it (feature 845627), 36.90384° N, 116.82924° W |
| Satellite | The satellite base map, credited on the map |
| The story | Jorge Luis Borges, *Del rigor en la ciencia* (On Exactitude in Science), 1946 |
| Built by | `datasets/borges/build.sh` in [pacha-dashboards](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/pacha-dashboards) |

spec.rawSql:
-- The sheet itself: the USGS scan clipped at its neatline, drawn by Pacha's tile server over the satellite.
SELECT 'http://feeds/datasets/borges/empire-1908.tif' AS raster_url

-- Where the next, more detailed map lies on this one: its neatline, a quarter of this sheet.
SELECT '{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[' || west || ',' || south || '],[' || east || ',' || south || '],['
         || east || ',' || north || '],[' || west || ',' || north || '],[' || west || ',' || south || ']]]}' AS geojson
FROM $sheets WHERE level = 'province'

-- Rhyolite where the USGS's Geographic Names Information System puts it (feature 845627): the same mark on every map.
SELECT 36.90384 AS latitude, -116.82924 AS longitude, 'Rhyolite' AS label

-- The next map's name, at the north-west corner of its frame.
SELECT north AS latitude, west AS longitude,
       quadrangle || ', ' || year::INTEGER || '  ·  1:' || format('{:,}', scale::BIGINT) AS label
FROM $sheets WHERE level = 'province'

spec.description: The USGS sheet clipped at its neatline over the satellite base map. The yellow frame is the next sheet of the ladder, a quarter of this one. The magenta ring is Rhyolite, at the same spot on every map of the ladder.
spec.title: Furnace Creek, 1908: the sheet, at its place

options.content:
**Furnace Creek, 1908.** One degree of desert across Nevada and California, with Death Valley along its western edge.

In 1908 Rhyolite, near the top of the sheet, was three years old: a gold town of a few thousand people, reached by three railways.

In Borges' story *On Exactitude in Science*, the cartographers of an Empire are never satisfied: the map of a province comes to fill a city, and the map of the Empire a province. These five dashboards go down that ladder. Each map is a quarter of the one before, printed on about the same sheet of paper; the yellow frame is the next one.
